consumer_contract.trust: t_start/t_end (frame-accurate, PySceneDetect, 0 of 234 values off the 1/25s grid, 10701/10701 frames covered), shot ordering and contiguity, words[] and word timing (joined by time window not index - structurally immune), keyframe paths (ffmpeg-verified on 3 shots), schema shape (3 validators), and the caption CORPUS as searchable content.
consumer_contract.do_not_trust: That shots[i].caption describes shots[i] - ~60% reliable, 58 of 102 graded pairs clean over six p3 runs. editorial_score and is_candidate on a NAMED shot inherit the same error (shot_059 was top-scored 0.85 on an empty-boot frame). 'What happens at 4:10' answered from the caption alone. The model's t_start_hint/t_end_hint as a self-check (hint_drift 0-1/117 on runs two-thirds wrong).
consumer_contract.rule_of_thumb: Corpus-level and aggregate use is safe. Per-shot editorial use requires checking the keyframe first. seed=7 makes a bad index stably bad, not intermittently bad - re-running does not shake it loose.

superseded_next_task_from_session_009: T011 has no cheap lever left. Both D-027 hypotheses are measured and the prompt/fps route is exhausted. The ONE untested class of fix is a different question, not a different prompt: merge adjacent sub-2s shots before the call (via --threshold) so the model chooses among ~60 distinguishable intervals instead of 117 near-identical ones. That changes shots[] itself, so it is a product decision and belongs in a NEW task (/new-task), not in T011. Alternative: accept the measured ~60% ceiling, close T011 as partial-by-design, and write the A/B up honestly. Budget any live session in REQUESTS (20/day, D-031), not tokens.
